assessment.summary: Cuba's CimaVax-EGF lung cancer vaccine exists, but the claim is refuted because the FDA authorized US trial access in October 2016, OFAC rule changes enabled access to Cuban-origin pharmaceuticals, and the US prescription barrier stems from FDA non-approval rather than sanctions.

evidence.finding: CimaVax-EGF is a therapeutic anticancer vaccine developed entirely in Cuba and licensed there for stage IIIB/IV non-small-cell lung cancer.
The FDA authorized Roswell Park to run a Phase I/II trial of CimaVAX in late October 2016, with nearly 200 US volunteers by mid-November, so the US did have access as of the reference date.
American doctors cannot prescribe CimaVax because the FDA has not approved it pending US trials, contradicting the claim's attribution of the access barrier to sanctions.

OFAC's October 2016 regulatory changes authorized transactions to obtain FDA approval of, and import and market, Cuban-origin pharmaceuticals, showing sanctions were modified to enable access rather than bar it.

assertions.assertion: Cuba has a lung cancer vaccine that the US had no access to because it sanctioned Cuba.

gaps: No FDA announcement or ClinicalTrials.gov registration was retrieved to independently confirm the trial authorization beyond secondary reports (S1, S3, S8).
The pre-October-2016 embargo bar on US citizens seeking medical treatment in Cuba (S1 P1) lacks primary regulation text, so the historical 'no access' window cannot be fully bounded.
contradictions: S1 P1 states the embargo forbids US citizens from seeking medical treatment in Cuba, partially supporting a historically bounded 'no access,' while S1 P2 and S5 record FDA/OFAC-enabled access from October 2016, refuting the unqualified claim for the reference date.
next_queries: ClinicalTrials.gov registration and status of the Roswell Park CimaVax-EGF phase I/II trial.
OFAC CACR provision text on medical treatment and Cuban-origin pharmaceuticals before and after October 2016.
FDA approval status of CimaVax-EGF as of February 2020.
